signals.title: All-cargo operator movements
signals.where: Air China Cargo, European Air Transport, China Cargo Airlines, ASL Airlines Belgium
signals.interpretation: Freighter movements are the observation closest to trade flow. Sustained change in this count would be the most economically meaningful signal this antenna can produce.
signals.caveat: Only 243 flights so far. Far too few to support any claim about trade. Included to establish the baseline, not to draw a conclusion.
signals.sql:
SELECT airline_prefix, COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights
WHERE airline_prefix IN ('FDX','UPS','GTI','CLX','CKS','ABW','CAO','CKK','GEC','BOX')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

signals.title: The working week barely changes how much flies — it changes what
signals.comparison: 1,401 flights a weekday vs 1,330 at the weekend
signals.interpretation: The total is almost flat, which is what you would expect over a point that mostly sees aircraft at cruise. Underneath it the mix moves hard in both directions: freight runs +80% on weekdays while charter runs -23%. Averaging a Tuesday with a Sunday cancels the two against each other and reports nothing. The composition is the signal; the count is not.
signals.caveat: One week. This describes the shape of a week, not a change in it — that needs a second week to compare against.
signals.sql:
SELECT daytype, carrier_kind, COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights
WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-08-30' AND '2026-09-05'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;

signals.title: Freight keeps office hours
signals.comparison: 36.0 a weekday vs 20.0 at the weekend
signals.where: Mon 30 → Tue 35 → Wed 37 → Thu 41 → Fri 37 → Sat 22 → Sun 18
signals.interpretation: Freighters follow the working week of the businesses that load them, and the count climbs through it before easing on Friday. This is the closest thing overhead to a trade figure: it is capacity moving because somebody has goods to move.
signals.caveat: Cargo is attributed by operator, not by aircraft. A freighter flown by a passenger airline is not counted here, and belly freight under passengers is invisible to us entirely.
signals.sql:
SELECT dow, COUNT(*) AS freight_flights
FROM flights
WHERE carrier_kind = 'cargo'
  AND day BETWEEN '2026-08-30' AND '2026-09-05'
GROUP BY 1;

signals.title: Busiest full day observed: 2026-09-03
signals.comparison: vs 1,345 average across 7 other full days
signals.interpretation: Day-to-day variation at this stage reflects weather, receiver uptime and normal schedule variation as much as anything about demand.
signals.caveat: Partial days are excluded from this comparison.

signals.title: Most aircraft overhead are not Nordic-registered
signals.interpretation: Aarhus sits beneath routings between Northern Europe and the rest of the world. A large non-Nordic share is evidence the antenna is seeing corridor traffic, not just local movements.
signals.caveat: Registration country is where an aircraft is registered — not where the flight began or where it is going.
signals.sql:
SELECT reg_country, COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

signals.title: China-registered aircraft crossing overhead
signals.interpretation: China has no scheduled service to Aarhus. These are aircraft at cruise altitude on intercontinental routings that happen to pass through this antenna's range. The count is a proxy for how busy that corridor is.
signals.caveat: Corridor routings shift with winds, airspace closures and slot times. Volume here is not the same as trade or passenger volume.

signals.title: Wide-body share of traffic
signals.interpretation: Wide-body airframes indicate long-haul routings. Tracking this share separately from the flight count matters: the same number of flights carrying larger aircraft is more capacity, not flat activity.
signals.caveat: Airframe type is identified from the aircraft's registered type code. It does not tell us the cabin configuration or how full it is.
signals.sql:
SELECT ac_type, ac_desc, COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights
WHERE ac_type SIMILAR TO '(A33|A35|A38|B74|B77|B78).*'
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;

signals.title: 1 wide-body type seen exactly once
signals.interpretation: Single appearances of long-haul airframes are usually charters, repositioning flights, or routings diverted off their usual track.
signals.caveat: One observation is an anecdote. These are listed because they are interesting, not because they mean anything yet.
signals.sql:
SELECT ac_type, ac_desc, callsign, seen_at
FROM flights
WHERE ac_type IN (SELECT ac_type FROM flights
                  GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
ORDER BY first_seen DESC;

signals.title: Holiday flying is a weekend business
signals.comparison: 23.5 a weekend day vs 18.2 on a weekday
signals.interpretation: Tour-operator flying is the purest leisure demand in the record — it exists because somebody booked a holiday. It runs opposite to freight, which is why the two cancel in the headline count.
signals.caveat: Only 138 charter flights in the week. The direction is clear; the size of it is not, at this sample.
signals.sql:
SELECT dow, COUNT(*) AS charter_flights
FROM flights
WHERE carrier_kind = 'leisure'
  AND day BETWEEN '2026-08-30' AND '2026-09-05'
GROUP BY 1;

signals.title: United Arab Em.-registered traffic up 220%
signals.interpretation: Movement in United Arab Em.-registered aircraft can reflect schedule changes, aircraft rotation, weather routing, or genuine changes in activity. At this sample size the first three are more likely.
signals.caveat: A 24-hour comparison on a few days of history is noise-dominated. Treat as something to watch, not a finding.
signals.sql:
SELECT strftime(seen_at, '%Y-%m-%d') AS day,
       COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights WHERE reg_country = 'AE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

signals.title: Austria-registered traffic down 52%
signals.interpretation: Movement in Austria-registered aircraft can reflect schedule changes, aircraft rotation, weather routing, or genuine changes in activity. At this sample size the first three are more likely.
signals.caveat: A 24-hour comparison on a few days of history is noise-dominated. Treat as something to watch, not a finding.

signals.title: United Kingdom-registered traffic down 51%
signals.interpretation: Movement in United Kingdom-registered aircraft can reflect schedule changes, aircraft rotation, weather routing, or genuine changes in activity. At this sample size the first three are more likely.
signals.caveat: A 24-hour comparison on a few days of history is noise-dominated. Treat as something to watch, not a finding.

       COUNT(*) AS flights
FROM flights WHERE reg_country = 'GB'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
